# Baghdad 830 – Tools, machines & manufacturing

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from eras/islamic-830-baghdad.yaml — do not edit -->

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Pulleys, block and tackle, treadwheel crane** [`block_and_tackle`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/block_and_tackle.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Pulleys, windlasses and capstans are ordinary on building sites, wells and ships. Heron's Mechanics on the five simple machines circulates in Greek; the big treadwheel crane is not a feature of Baghdad sites, where brick is carried up on backs and ramps. Local: brick-builders of the palaces at Shammasiyya and Rusafa; boatmen and porters on the Tigris quays.
- **Wheelbarrow** [`wheelbarrow`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wheelbarrow.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Loads go by donkey, camel, mule, porter and basket. Wheeled carts are rare in the caliphate, where pack animals have long since replaced them; a one-wheeled barrow would be new and useful on brick and canal works. Local: canal diggers on the Nahr Isa and Sarat. Elsewhere: China (wheelbarrows since Han times).
- **Archimedes' screw (water screw)** [`archimedes_screw`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/archimedes_screw.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Known from Greek and Egyptian practice; the Egyptian Delta still uses it. In Iraq water is lifted by shaduf, by animal-driven saqiya chains of pots and by current-driven norias. Elsewhere: Egypt (water screws in the Delta).
- **Gears and gear trains** [`gears_gear_trains`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/gears_gear_trains.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. The right-angle gear of the saqiya is in every irrigated field. Geared trains survive only in Greek descriptions (Heron, Philo); the Banu Musa will build trick vessels and automata around 850, without gear trains of any precision. Local: saqiya wheelwrights in the Sawad; the Banu Musa (young, collecting Greek mechanical books). Elsewhere: Constantinople (throne automata, usually attributed to Theophilos).
- **Cam and camshaft** [`cam_camshaft`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cam_camshaft.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept medium. Pegs on a rotating drum appear in Heron's automata texts. No cam-driven machine is at work in Iraq. Elsewhere: China (water-powered trip hammers since Han times).
- **Screw, nut and bolt** [`screw_nut_bolt`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/screw_nut_bolt.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept medium. The wooden screw press for oil and grapes is a Greek and Roman device known in Syria. Metal screws and nuts are unknown; joints are pegged, riveted or lashed. Elsewhere: Syria and Byzantium (wooden screw presses).
- **Belt, rope and chain drives** [`belt_drive`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/belt_drive.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Bow drills and bow lathes use a cord; the chain of pots on the saqiya is the main endless chain. A driven belt between two wheels for spinning or grinding is not in use. Local: turners and bead drillers in the Karkh suqs. Elsewhere: China (belt-driven quilling wheels).
- **Ball and roller bearings** [`ball_bearings`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/ball_bearings.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Axles turn in wooden or bronze sockets greased with fat or oil. Rollers under heavy stones are known to builders.
- **Bellows and the double-acting piston blower** [`bellows_piston_blower`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bellows_piston_blower.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Smiths, glassmakers and crucible-steel makers work goat-skin bellows by hand or foot. A double-acting piston blower is unknown here. Local: smiths of the Suq al-Haddadin. Elsewhere: China (piston bellows, water-powered blowers).
- **Water-powered trip hammer and stamp mill** [`trip_hammer_water_powered`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/trip_hammer_water_powered.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Paper pulp is beaten by hand or with foot-worked hammers; water-driven stamps for paper are claimed for the Islamic world only later and their extent is debated. The Tigris and the big canals give power where boat mills already grind grain. Local: paper makers of Baghdad. Elsewhere: China (water-powered trip hammers since about AD 20).
- **Lost-wax casting** [`lost_wax_casting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lost_wax_casting.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Bronze and brass ewers, incense burners, lamps and figured spouts are cast by lost wax in Iraq, Iran and Egypt, continuing Sasanian and Byzantine practice. Local: coppersmiths and brass founders of Baghdad and Basra.
- **Sand and loam moulding for large castings** [`sand_loam_casting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sand_loam_casting.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Nothing large is cast here; churches under Muslim rule call to prayer with the naqus, a wooden clapper or a small bell, struck softly. Coins are struck, not cast. Loam moulds for a big casting would need a founder from Byzantium or Khurasan.
- **Wire drawing** [`wire_drawing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wire_drawing.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Gold and silver thread for brocade and tiraz bands is drawn and wrapped round silk; mail-makers need iron wire. Draw-plates are a craft secret of a few workshops. Local: tiraz workshops (state textile factories) supplying robes of honour; mail-makers for the Khurasani army.
- **Rolling and slitting mill** [`rolling_mill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/rolling_mill.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Sheet metal is hammered; coin blanks are cast and struck by hand at the Baghdad mint. Local: Madinat al-Salam mint (dar al-darb).
- **Precision cylinder boring** [`boring_machine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/boring_machine.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Nothing needs a true cylinder. Copper pipes for fountains are hammered and soldered; the bore of a force pump in Heron's book is the only model.
- **Screw-cutting lathe with slide rest** [`lathe_screw_cutting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lathe_screw_cutting.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept low. Bow lathes turn wood, ivory and soft stone. A slide rest and lead screw are unknown. Local: ivory and wood turners in the suqs.
- **Precision measurement (flat surfaces, gauges, micrometer)** [`precision_measurement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/precision_measurement.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Assayers and mint officials weigh to fractions of a grain; astronomers divide large brass rings to minutes of arc. Lengths are cubits that differ by trade (the black cubit, the cubit of the cloth trade). Local: Sanad ibn Ali and Ali ibn Isa al-Asturlabi (instrument makers); mint assayers.
- **Machine tools (planer, shaper, milling machine)** [`machine_tools`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/machine_tools.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low
- **Interchangeable parts** [`interchangeable_parts`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/interchangeable_parts.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Arrows, nails and coins are made in large numbers but fitted by hand. Coin dies and glass coin weights are the nearest thing to a standard part.
- **Assembly line and mass production** [`assembly_line`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/assembly_line.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. The state tiraz workshops and the paper mills divide work among many hands, and copyists in the Suq al-Warraqin split a book into quires among several scribes. Nobody organises this as a principle. Local: Suq al-Warraqin (stationers' and copyists' market).
- **Water-powered sawmill** [`sawmill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sawmill.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Timber is scarce and imported (teak from India for ships, wood from the north by river); sawyers cut by hand. Water saws are reported only later, and thinly, from al-Andalus.
- **Spinning wheel** [`spinning_wheel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spinning_wheel.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Cotton, flax, wool and silk are spun with the hand spindle and distaff, mostly by women at home. The spinning wheel is first securely attested around 1000, and where it was invented is disputed. Elsewhere: China (silk-reeling and quilling wheels); India (roller gins; wheel origin claimed but unproven).
- **Spinning machines (jenny, water frame, mule)** [`spinning_machines`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spinning_machines.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low
- **Horizontal treadle loom** [`treadle_loom`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/treadle_loom.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Pit treadle looms for cotton and linen and draw looms for patterned silk work in Iraq, Khuzistan and Iran. Textiles are the caliphate's great industry and a court currency (robes of honour). Local: tiraz workshops; weavers of Tustar and Sus in Khuzistan.
- **Flying shuttle and power loom** [`power_loom`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/power_loom.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low
- **Cotton gin** [`cotton_gin`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cotton_gin.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept high. Cotton is spreading in Iraq and Iran, cleaned by hand or with an Indian-style roller worked on a flat stone. A cranked two-roller gin would double a worker's output with the same carpenters. Elsewhere: India (roller gins since early centuries AD).
- **Stocking frame (knitting machine)** [`knitting_frame`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/knitting_frame.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. True knitting is not yet attested; socks are sewn from cloth or made by needle-looping.
